Disclosed exceptions: (1) B4's window was set by the task at 2026-09-21T20:12:16Z, so its one alarm so far (HYPE 09-21 18:15 ET, belief 0.230, a caught loser) was known; (2) while measuring event rates at 13:26Z a sizing script also printed post-freeze COUNTS for the first 7 closes: 1 fresh-offer 45 s close, 0 older, 0 flagged fills, 0 alarms, 131 contracts bought at <=30 s. No threshold was moved toward those counts; B5's reference was made STRICTER, not looser, after it.

code_after.note: bug/safety fixes and logging only; no flag changed

may_change: safety fixes (the hedge must always be able to run)
each versioned in results/VERSIONS.md at deploy
may_not_change: any entry gate, size, price limit or hedge trigger
freeze.close_counts_if: close_s >= start + 60 s and (the live bot logged a close_summary for it, or Kalshi's ledger holds a pin market settling at it); held back while a market we filled in it has no ledger result

multiple_looks.summary: Each decision bar decides once, on its first registered n; only B1-B3 are discovery tests and their false-PASS rates with nothing real sum to <= 0.08.
multiple_looks.within_bar: A decision bar is computed ONCE, on a fixed sample: the first N units (closes / events / alarms) in time order after its window opens. Before N it is COLLECTING and its running numbers decide nothing. After N the verdict is fixed; later data is report only. Re-running barcheck cannot turn a FAIL into a PASS.
multiple_looks.restart_rule: If a live start record after a bar's window opens differs from the config in force at the window start on any of the bar's config_keys, the bar's window restarts at that record. Samples are never pooled across settings. A code-only change (bug fix) does not restart a bar.
multiple_looks.null_false_pass_basis: B1: resampled P >= 0.975 is a one-sided 2.5% level per policy (raised from the draft's 0.90 for this family); the effect floors ($0.50 / $0.25 a close) are at z 1.6-2.7 with the measured sd, so 2.5% is the worst case. B2, B3: simulated 4,000 null worlds at the registered n (Fisher exact is conservative at these counts: nominal 0.05 gives 0.009 at 80 v 80 and 0.019 at 20 v 300); each bar ALSO needs its dollar condition, which can only lower these.

not_in_family.B4: a burden-of-proof bar on a setting that went live without passing its own registered bar (v-hedge25 bypassed PREREG's 'not below 0.30'). PASS keeps 0.25; FAIL returns to PREREG's floor 0.30 (or the leader). It cannot discover a new setting -- both alternatives are earlier states. Its guard is PREREG's own: no single event > half the difference. Its safety half is PREREG's n=30 rules, a stop rule, not a discovery.
not_in_family.B5: descriptive; names a cause at most; never changes the bot by itself -- a named cause becomes a written proposal needing its own pre-registered bar
not_in_family.B6: report only; never a deployment trigger

multiple_looks.interim: status/brief lines show counts before n; running dollar comparisons appear only in FREEZE_status.md detail, labelled report-only

bars.title: 45 s leg: a third (live) vs full vs off
bars.question: Over the freeze, would the 45 s leg at full size, or off, have made more than the third that ran?
bars.data: Kalshi ledger (pinledger.pnl per market) for LIVE; research/earlyhindsight.py's per-close counterfactual for FULL and OFF, built from live order records (order: filled, exec_price, limit_sent, leg, tau_at_send, fee_total), their signal records (size, ladder, level at decision), sweep_depth (ladder), hedge records (side, n, price, ladder_n, ask_size), start/autosize (size, early_frac). No tape, no replay.
bars.statistic: per close, d_p = policy_p - live (dollars); mean of d_p over the first 300 closes; resampled P(sum d_p > 0) over closes (10,000 draws); largest single close's share of the total gain

scorer.pipeline: load_ledger -> load_live_runs -> extract -> score(ledger, fills, hedges, lo, hi, {full: FULL, off: 0.0}); rows {close, live, pol{full, off}}
scorer.row_contract: one row per close: close (UTC epoch s), live, full, off (flat or under pol) -- WHOLE-CLOSE dollars under each policy; live must equal Kalshi's ledger for that close

bars.decision: PASS (switch to the passing policy; both pass -> the larger mean) if, on the first 300 closes: mean gain >= its floor AND resampled P >= 0.975 AND no single close > 50% of the gain AND the scorer's live column reconciles to Kalshi within max($1, 2%) with no 45 s-leg close missing a row. FAIL (keep the third) otherwise at 300. COLLECTING before 300. INVALID if it does not reconcile. PENDING while earlyhindsight is not importable.
bars.mde: Per-close sd of the 45 s leg's ledger P&L, pre-freeze (reproduced here): $4.81 (09-20 04Z..T0, 216 closes) to $7.94 (09-17 13:05Z..T0, 465 closes). full - third = 2/3 of the leg, off - third = -1/3. At 300 closes, one-sided 2.5%, 80% power: full $0.52-$0.86 a close, off $0.26-$0.43 a close. A real difference smaller than that will most likely read FAIL: FAIL means 'not shown', not 'no difference'.
bars.on_pass: put the switch to the operator (off = drop the four early flags; full = --early-frac 1.0); if he agrees, a versioned change after the freeze
bars.on_fail: keep the third; report the three-way ranking once
bars.on_collecting: counts only in --brief; the running ranking sits in FREEZE_status.md detail and decides nothing
bars.blocks: nothing: it changes a size, never a gate; hedges size to whatever is held

bars.title: fresh-offer rule on the 45 s leg (map C5), out of sample
bars.question: Do 45 s-leg buys on offers under 250 ms old lose more closes than buys on older offers, out of sample -- enough that refusing them would have saved money?
bars.data: order records with leg == early and filled > 0 (ticker, want, filled, t), each paired with its signal record <= 3 s before (level_age_ms); Kalshi ledger per market (market_result, pinledger.pnl). A market is 'fresh' if every 45 s fill was on a level < 250 ms old, 'older' if none was; mixed or missing age is not classed (counted).
bars.statistic: closes in each group; a close is lost if a market in the group lost (result != want). One-sided Fisher exact test fresh > older. Dollars: minus the fresh markets' ledger P&L pro-rated by the 45 s leg's share of the contracts, resampled over closes.
bars.decision: Sample = closes in time order until both groups hold >= 80. PASS if fresh lose more often AND Fisher p <= 0.05 AND refusing fresh would have kept > $0 with resampled P >= 0.90. FAIL at the sample otherwise. COLLECTING before.
bars.mde: Pre-freeze rates: ~13-15 fresh and ~15-21 older 45 s closes a day, so ~6 days (~570 closes), past the 300-close freeze. Power at 80 v 80, Fisher 0.05 (simulated): 0.69 for C5's in-sample 8.2% v 0.5%, 0.44 for 7% v 1%, 0.21 for 5% v 1%. False PASS with nothing real: 0.009. A FAIL here is weak evidence of no effect.
bars.on_pass: propose a gate refusing 45 s-leg ENTRIES on offer levels < 250 ms old -- operator's call, versioned, after the freeze, with its own undo bar
bars.on_fail: C5 closed as in-sample noise; no gate
bars.blocks: if adopted: ONLY 45 s-leg ENTRIES on levels < 250 ms old. Never a <=30 s entry, never a hedge.
touches: any change to the early leg's entry gates

bars.title: post-fill collapse as a HEDGE trigger (map C6), priced
bars.question: When a fill lands >= 2c below the ask we saw (the book moved while our order flew), would buying insurance at once have saved money, net of what it costs on the ones that win?
bars.window_note: the per-second insurance log (hedge_quote) exists only from v-safety1; the window opens at the first hedge_quote record
needs_fields: hedge_quote (ticker, side, ask, size, tau, belief), one per held market per second
bars.data: order records (exec_price, ask_seen, want, filled, t); hedge_quote records for the same ticker (ask, size, t); hedge records (side, price, n, live); Kalshi ledger per market (market_result).
bars.statistic: flagged close = a fill with exec_price <= ask_seen - 0.02. Loss rate flagged v other closes (one-sided Fisher). Value per flagged close = insurance bought from our own logged quotes, one try a second for 30 s from the fill's second, min(held, quoted size) at the quoted ask < $1, fee included, MINUS the hedge legs that actually ran after the fill; resampled over flagged closes.
bars.decision: Sample = settled closes in time order until 20 flagged closes are priced. PASS if flagged lose more often AND Fisher p <= 0.05 AND value > $0 with resampled P >= 0.90 AND no single close > 50% of the value. FAIL at the sample otherwise. COLLECTING before. PENDING without hedge_quote.
bars.mde: ~2.1-2.2 flagged closes a day pre-freeze, so ~9-10 days. Replication power at 20 flagged v ~400 other, Fisher 0.05 (simulated): 0.93 for C6's 26% v 2.3%, 0.61 for 15% v 2.3%; false PASS 0.019. Value: at ~10c insurance on ~78 contracts, SE ~$7.7 a flagged close; break-even loss rate ~10%; at C6's 26% the expected value is ~+$12.5 a flagged close and P >= 0.90 is reached ~64% of the time.
bars.on_pass: propose an immediate hedge on fills >= 2c below the ask seen -- operator's call, versioned, after the freeze
bars.on_collecting: LOG ONLY: nothing trades on this signal
bars.blocks: nothing: it would ADD a hedge. It must never use the belief hedge's retry budget or trip the pintake halt.

bars.title: hedge trigger 0.25 (v-hedge25) against PREREG_hedge.md's bar, restored
bars.question: Has the 0.25 trigger earned its place under the hedge pre-registration it bypassed: ahead of 0.30 (the registered floor) and 0.60 (what it replaced), and inside PREREG's four safety rules?
needs_fields: hedge_quote records with belief (move bar only)
bars.data: (a) safety: hedge_alarm (ticker, want, t), hedge (ticker, side, price, n, live), order fills (positions held), Kalshi ledger (market_result). (b) move bar: an EVENT is a held position whose logged hedge_quote belief fell below 0.60 at any second after its first fill; hedge_quote (ask, size, belief) prices the insurance each trigger would have bought.
bars.statistic: (a) PREREG's four rules over the FIRST 30 alarms: false alarms / positions held up to the 30th alarm; mean money back per hedged contract on caught losers (100 - price c); share of alarms with a hedge fill; any hedge at >= $1.00. (b) per event and trigger th in {0.25, 0.30, 0.60}: dollars from the insurance leg bought at the first second belief < th, one try a second for 30 s at the quoted ask/size; sum over the first 10 events of (0.25 - th); largest single event's share.
bars.decision: Move bar (PREREG 09-14 wording, restored): on the first 10 settled events after the quote log began, PASS if 0.25 is ahead of BOTH 0.30 and 0.60 in total, each lead with no single event > 50% of it; FAIL otherwise (a tie is not a lead). Safety (PREREG 09-12): on the first 30 alarms, PASS if false alarms <= 3% of positions held, money back >= 25c a contract, fill >= 60%; FAIL if any rule misses, and at ANY n if a hedge ever cost >= $1.00. The bar's status is FAIL if either half fails.
bars.mde: Dips below 60% ran ~1.9 a day pre-freeze (alarms under the 0.60 trigger), so 10 events is ~5 days once quotes are logged (from 11:52Z). The safety bar's 30 real alarms at 0.25 is ~3-5 weeks (0.9-1.5 alarms a day). No power statement for the move bar: it is a burden-of-proof rule, not a test.
bars.on_pass: 0.25 stays, now inside PREREG's rules; next safety review at 100 alarms
bars.on_fail: Safety FAIL: PREREG says disable the hedge, but the operator's standing 09-14 order is 'Keep the hedge', so it goes to him as a decision. Move FAIL: put to the operator a return to 0.30 (PREREG's floor), or to 0.60 if 0.60 led -- a strategy change, so his call, versioned, after the freeze.
bars.blocks: nothing: a trigger level, never a gate. The hedge path, its retries and its bypass of the pintake halt stay as they are.

bars.title: why the <=30 s window's volume fell 65% (critic G2)
bars.question: The <=30 s window bought 2,654 contracts a day in era B and 936 after the fixes while supply was flat. Is it (a) back now the 45 s leg is a third, (b) the offers not being there at our price, or (c) one of our own gates / the close budget?
bars.window_note: tau and budget_left on every refusal exist only from v-safety1; the window opens at the first such refusal
needs_fields: tau and budget_left on every refused record
bars.data: order records (filled, leg, tau_at_send) for contracts bought at <= 30 s; refused records (gate, close_s, tau, budget_left, size_now, and the price each gate writes: no_offer wanted_side + <side>_ask / <side>_ask_size; book gates want + price + size, depth_floor also offered; capacity gates none) -- first refusal per (close, market, gate), so an undercount; close_summary for the close count.
bars.statistic: per watched close: contracts bought at <= 30 s outside the 45 s leg; refused contracts, refusals with 3-30 s left only: PRICED refusals with our side at 90-98c count min(offered, size_now); UNPRICED refusals from a capacity gate (unpriced_gates: refused before the book was read) count size_now, an upper bound; other unpriced refusals and our side outside 90-98c are dropped and counted. Classed by gate ('budget used up' when budget_left <= 0); gap = reference - bought.
bars.correction: The 13:37Z version read only no_offer's field names (wanted_side, <side>_ask), so it would have dropped every book-gate refusal (want/price/size/offered) and every capacity-gate refusal (no price): on the first real run it kept 0 of 134 and would have answered (b) 'the offers were not there' by construction. Fixed as a reader bug before 100 closes; thresholds, reference, sample sizes and answers (a)-(c) unchanged. Capacity gates are counted at our size (an upper bound) because they refuse before the book is read -- including close_budget, the hypothesis B5 exists to test. Seen before fixing: the first 7 closes' refusal COUNTS by gate (no_offer 15, edge_floor 5, depth_floor 5, price_ceiling 3, book_stale 2, rebuy_band 1, max_per_market 1), no volumes.

own_measured_pre_freeze.note: by fill time, 13:2xZ sizing script; barcheck recomputes by close time at every run

bars.decision: Reference = the STRICTER (higher) of map 11's 2,654/day as 27.65 a close (/96) and this file's own era-B count. On the first 100 closes, then (if no answer) the first 300: ANSWER (PASS) = (a) bought >= 80% of the reference; else (b) refused (priced + unpriced upper bound) < 50% of the gap; else (c) one cause holds >= 50% of the refused volume and refused covers >= 80% of the gap. NO ANSWER (FAIL) at 300: report the top three causes. COLLECTING before 100. PENDING without the fields.
bars.mde: descriptive: a share of refused volume, not a test. 100 closes is ~1 day.
bars.on_pass: the named cause becomes a written proposal for after the freeze, with its own pre-registered bar; no gate is loosened on this alone
bars.on_fail: no single cause; the report lists the top three

bars.title: paper arms vs live on shared closes
bars.question: For each practice bot, on closes it and live both watched on the same code: did its one changed setting trade different markets, and how did its paper money compare with Kalshi's?
bars.code_rule: a close is shared only if the arm's run and the live run in force 60 s before the close carry the same code_sha (live moved to v-safety1 at 11:52:44Z; the arms at 12:01Z)
bars.data: paper logs pinrun-paper-*.jsonl (start: every flag + code_sha; close_summary; signal live=false take_n; settled pnl_c, exact duplicates once), arm-*.out for names; live start records (code_sha) and close_summary; Kalshi ledger per close.
bars.statistic: per arm: shared closes; arm paper dollars and c/contract; live ledger dollars and c/contract; markets both / arm only / live only (zero differences = the flag never changed a trade).
bars.decision: REPORT only, from 50 shared closes. Never PASS or FAIL.
bars.mde: none: report only (paper fills are not our fills)
bars.on_pass: never: an arm alone never triggers a deployment
